questions.prompt: In RFM analysis, what does the 'R' stand for?
questions.explanation: R in RFM stands for Recency, indicating how recently a customer made a purchase.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best describes the primary difference between demographic and behavioral segmentation?

options.text: Demographic segmentation is based on customer actions, while behavioral segmentation uses age and income.
Demographic segmentation uses age, income, and education, whereas behavioral segmentation focuses on purchase frequency and brand loyalty.
Both use the same data but different analysis tools.
Demographic segmentation is only for B2B markets.

questions.explanation: Demographic segmentation classifies customers by static attributes like age and income, whereas behavioral segmentation groups them based on actions such as purchase frequency and loyalty.

questions.prompt: When performing K-means clustering for customer segmentation, which distance metric is most commonly used?
questions.explanation: K-means relies on Euclidean distance to assign points to the nearest cluster centroid.

questions.prompt: Why is it beneficial to segment customers by lifetime value (LTV)?

options.text: It identifies which customers are most profitable over time.
It replaces the need for demographic data.

questions.explanation: Segmenting by LTV highlights high‑value customers, allowing focused investment in retention and upsell.

questions.prompt: A retailer notices that a particular segment has high purchase frequency but low average order value. Which retention strategy is most appropriate?

options.text: Offer high‑margin product bundles to increase order value.
Reduce marketing spend on the segment.
Provide loyalty points that reward large orders.
Replace the product assortment with premium items.

questions.explanation: Bundling encourages customers to add more items per visit, boosting average order value while maintaining frequency.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a common pitfall when creating customer segments?

options.text: Using too few data points per segment.

questions.explanation: Small sample sizes produce unreliable clusters that can mislead targeting decisions.
